newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE SHARE INDEX UP AS LOCAL TRANCHES RALLY.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE SHARE INDEX UP AS LOCAL TRANCHES RALLY.

text.p: Singapore's benchmark share index rallied on Thursday morning after a government-owned group of companies said it was merging its foreign and local share tranches, boosting other local blue chip stock tranches.
By 0220 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was up 22.10 points at 1,897.48. Trading was brisk with some 56 million shares changing hands in the first hour.
The unweighted 30-share index contains the local tranches of Singapore Airlines (SIA) and Singapore Press. Both rallied on news that the Singapore Technologies group was merging its share tranches.

Foreign tranches traditionally hold a premium over local tranches because they can be bought by any investor and tend to be much more volatile. Scrapping of the split between the tranches would remove this price differential.
SIA foreign was down 40 cents at Singapore $12.00 and the local tranche was up 40 cents at S$8.00.
Singapore Press foreign was down 70 cents at S$25.70 while its local tranche was up 40 cents at S$13.40.
Shares in compact disc-maker SM Summit Holdings Ltd rallied 9.5 cents to a high of S$0.75 after trading in its shares was allowed to resume following a half-day suspension.

The shares were suspended on Wednesday after they fell almost 38 percent to a low of S$0.655 after the company's offices were raided by police and industry officials on suspicion of illegal software manufacture.
SM Summit denied any wrongdoing after it and another local company were sued by U.S. giant Microsoft Corp and two other American software companies.
